title: Streaming halting & prefix-escape protocol for interleaved tool calls
creator: Anjali Patel
description:
Problem summary:

When clients stream structured JSON that contains interleaved tool/function calls, two frequent failure modes occur in production: (1) the model halts mid-entity because backpressure or connectivity triggers a truncation; (2) prefix-like content from earlier tool responses is misinterpreted as live JSON (escape ambiguity), causing downstream parsers to treat partial output as final. These failures produce non-idempotent retries, duplicated tool calls, or corrupted structured payloads.

This ticket defines a small, implementation-friendly protocol (protocol sketch + runtime changes) to reduce corruption and duplicate tool calls by: introducing an explicit "halting window" sentinel, a prefix-escape convention for embedded tool outputs, and an idempotent resume marker that is compact and compatible with existing streaming APIs. The protocol must be compatible with: our streaming SDKs, token-level cost tracking, function-call semantics (ensuring single invocation semantics on retries), and existing clients who expect LDJSON and chunked streaming.

Goals:
- Prevent accidental tool re-invocations on transient truncation/reconnects while preserving low-latency streaming.
- Ensure parsers can distinguish between escaped prefix fragments and live-generated structured fields.
- Keep runtime and SDK changes minimal and optional behind flags to allow gradual rollout.

Out of scope:
- Full redesign of tool-call idempotency at the application layer (we will provide primitives, not replace user-side idempotency keys).
- Changes to billing or token accounting beyond attaching small resume metadata headers.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming responses can include a compact halting sentinel sequence that marks a safe pause boundary; SDKs treat sentinel as non-final and will attempt resume negotiation unless a final 'end' marker follows.

When the runtime detects a resume, it must rehydrate the last acknowledged KV-cache prefix and replay token generation without re-invoking tool side-effects (function calls must be signalled as already-delivered).
A prefix-escape encoding is defined for embedding previous tool output or partial JSON that avoids ambiguity with live keys and reduces false-positives in downstream JSON parsers.
Protocol is backwards-compatible: clients that do not implement resume semantics simply receive sentinels as opaque tokens and still produce parseable LDJSON (no crashes).

End-to-end tests demonstrating: (a) reconnection after truncation without duplicate tool calls, (b) client that does not understand sentinel still produces a correct but less-optimized fallback result.
design_decisions: Sentinel design: choose a short, UTF-8 safe sequence prefixed with a configurable guard ('\u241E~R') to reduce collision with model output while keeping bandwidth low.

Resume negotiation: use a 1-RTT explicit resume header in the resume request (Resume-Token) rather than attempting token-level dedupe in transport layer to keep implementation portable across HTTP/WS/GRPC.

Tool-call marking: runtime annotates function-call events with an 'acknowledged' flag included in resume metadata; client SDK APIs will expose a boolean to indicate whether a tool's side-effect should be replayed.

Escape strategy: adopt 'length-prefixed fragments' for embedding prior tool outputs inside structured fields (e.g., "__escaped_fragment__": "<len>:<bytes>"), because JSON string escaping alone was unreliable across truncation boundaries.
Rollout: gate protocol behind runtime flag 'stream-halting-protocol-v1' and provide opt-in SDK helpers for Node/Python.
implementation_plan: Runtime changes (server): generate halting sentinel at safe emission points (end of top-level object or before a tool-call boundary); attach minimal resume metadata to streaming checkpoints.

SDK changes: Node/Python SDKs parse sentinel, surface resume token in reconnect helper, and provide helper to reconcile acknowledged tool calls; fall back to normal behavior when feature flag not present.
Function-call runtime: mark function-call events atomically in the stream and persist a lightweight 'call-ack' entry in the request-level transient store for resume verification.
API surface: document new optional headers (X-Resume-Token) and streaming markers in API docs; add examples for embedding escaped fragments and for reconnection flows.
Tests: add fuzz tests for sentinel collision, automated replay e2e tests with simulated network truncation, and unit tests for length-prefixed escape encoding/decoding.
test_plan: Unit tests for encoder/decoder of length-prefixed fragments including boundary conditions (empty fragment, max-length fragment truncated).
Integration tests that simulate mid-stream TCP disconnect and validate: (1) no duplicate tool function invocation, (2) correctness of final assembled JSON, (3) resume token verification path.
Contract tests: verify SDKs and server produce backwards-compatible LDJSON when sentinel present but client unaware.
Load test scenario: measure CPU/latency impact of sentinel insertion at 10K QPS for typical request size distribution to ensure overhead < 1.5% p50 latency increase.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Internal dogfood: enable feature flag for 10% of internal runtime capacity; SDKs use opt-in reconnection helpers. Monitor duplicate tool invocations and parser error rates.
Stage 2 - Beta partners: enable for sandbox and a small set of external customers with opt-in release notes and support runbook for debugging resume failures.
Stage 3 - Gradual ramp: increase to 50% with feature telemetry gating, then 100% if no regression in 72 hours. Deprecate fallback after 3 months of stable telemetry.
Provide a toggle to disable sentinels per-tenant to mitigate unexpected client-side breakage.
comments: 2025-03-10 Anjali Patel: Created ticket after incident where a reconnect caused two calls to the 'decode_image' function. Included initial protocol sketch and examples.

2025-03-11 Lucas Rivera: Spike completed; prototyped length-prefixed fragments and a short sentinel sequence. Found one collision with generated natural text in a small subset of prompts; mitigations noted in design decisions.
2025-03-12 Maya Chen: Reviewed design; requested that resume tokens be HMAC-signed to prevent client-side tampering. Marked as P1 due to customer impact on image-processing partner.
2025-03-12 Lucas Rivera: Implementing server-side call-ack persistence and adding unit tests for decoder. ETA for first dogfood build: 2025-03-17.
